title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: OZZIE'S MAGIC SHOW
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Ozzie Lindqvist, an iron ore dock worker in Marquette, Michigan.
He has hands like snow shovels.
Three weeks before Christmas, those hands had to do magic.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE ASK
segments.quote: We turn not older with years, but newer every day.
segments.author: Emily Dickinson
lines: His dad, Walt, lives at the Pine Ridge senior home, and hardly smiles lately.
Their magician, the Amazing Arnie, sprained his wrist and asked Ozzie to do the show.
Ozzie said, I'm forty-eight. Too old. Arnie, eighty-two, read him a line from Emily Dickinson:
We turn not older with years, but newer every day.
So Ozzie said yes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: BUTTERFINGERS
segments.quote: Every habit and faculty is confirmed and strengthened by the corresponding actions.
segments.author: Epictetus
lines: His first card trick sent fifty-two cards across the kitchen floor.
His wife found the jack of hearts in the dog bowl.
Arnie quoted the old Greek thinker Epictetus:
Every habit and faculty is confirmed and strengthened by the corresponding actions.
So Ozzie did tricks every day. Even in the shower, with soap.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: ARNIE'S SECRET
segments.quote: The greatest compliment that was ever paid me was when one asked me what I thought, and attended to my answer.
segments.author: Henry David Thoreau
lines: His moves got better, but his buddies looked bored.
Arnie said, Stop showing off. Look at the people.
Inside his top hat was a line from Henry David Thoreau:
The greatest compliment that was ever paid me was when one asked me what I thought, and attended to my answer.
So Ozzie learned names, asked questions, and listened.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE RUBBER CHICKEN
segments.quote: Be so good that they can't ignore you.
segments.author: Steve Martin
lines: At the dress rehearsal, his rubber chicken was supposed to vanish.
It dropped out of his pant leg. Plop.
Ozzie wanted to quit. Arnie quoted the comedian Steve Martin, who started with magic too:
Be so good that they can't ignore you.
So Ozzie practiced every night. The chicken stayed put.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: SHOW NIGHT
segments.quote: Men love to wonder, and that is the seed of our science.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: On show night, Walt sat in the front row, arms crossed.
Ozzie pulled a quarter from behind his ear. Walt said, How did you do that?
Ozzie almost told him. Then he remembered a line from Ralph Waldo Emerson:
Men love to wonder, and that is the seed of our science.
So he winked. And his dad laughed for the first time in months.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: EVERY OTHER SUNDAY
segments.quote: The universe is full of magical things patiently waiting for our wits to grow sharper.
segments.author: Eden Phillpotts
lines: Now Ozzie does a show every other Sunday, with Arnie assisting.
Walt sits up front and says, That's my boy.
Arnie gave Ozzie his top hat, with a card from the English novelist Eden Phillpotts:
The universe is full of magical things patiently waiting for our wits to grow sharper.
Ozzie sees them everywhere now.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Start new. Practice. Listen. Get better. Leave room for wonder. Look for magic.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Start new at any age. Practice daily. Listen. Get better after a flop. Leave room for wonder. Look for magic.
I tried a magic trick once. I made my lunch disappear. Twice.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
